name: Billy the Kid
summary: A young outlaw known for his charm and deadly gunfighting skills in the New Mexico Territory.

name: Wyatt Earp
summary: A complex figure who was a businessman, gambler, and lawman, most famously involved in the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

name: Doc Holliday
summary: A dentist turned gambler and gunfighter, known for his loyalty to Wyatt Earp and his quick draw.

name: Jesse James
summary: A notorious outlaw who led a gang in robberies across the Midwest and was romanticized as a folk hero.

name: Buffalo Bill Cody
summary: A bison hunter, army scout, and showman who popularized the image of the Wild West through his traveling show.

name: Annie Oakley
summary: A sharpshooter who gained fame in Buffalo Bill's Wild West show for her incredible marksmanship.

name: Calamity Jane
summary: A frontierswoman, known for her adventurous spirit, sharpshooting skills, and association with Wild Bill Hickok.

name: Davy Crockett
summary: A frontiersman, hunter, soldier, and politician who became a legendary figure known for his coonskin cap and bravery at the Alamo.

name: Butch Cassidy
summary: The charismatic leader of the Wild Bunch gang, known for their train and bank robberies across the West.

name: The Sundance Kid
summary: An outlaw and member of Butch Cassidy's Wild Bunch, often depicted as a skilled gunman.

name: Joaquín Murrieta
summary: A controversial figure, considered by some a bandit and by others a Mexican resistance hero against Anglo-American oppression in California.

name: La Llorona
summary: A legendary weeping woman who is said to roam waterfront areas, mourning the children she drowned.

name: El Charro Negro
summary: A feared apparition of a rider dressed in black on a black horse, often associated with deals with the devil.

name: Quetzalcoatl
summary: The Aztec feathered serpent god, a central figure in Mesoamerican mythology, credited with bringing knowledge and maize to humankind.

name: La Mulata de Córdoba
summary: A mysterious and beautiful woman in colonial Veracruz who was accused of witchcraft and vanished from prison.

name: The Legend of the Volcanoes (Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl)
summary: A tragic love story explaining the creation of the two famous volcanoes near Mexico City.

name: Pancho Villa
summary: A revolutionary general in the Mexican Revolution, known for his military tactics and raids on the US border.

name: Emiliano Zapata
summary: A leading figure in the Mexican Revolution, advocating for the rights of peasants and agrarian reform.

name: Tiburcio Vásquez
summary: A California bandit who, like Murrieta, was seen by some as a social bandit resisting American dominance.

name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
summary: The Virgin Mary as she appeared in Mexico, a powerful religious and cultural symbol for Mexicans.
